data.narrative:
Material Evolution, led by founders Liz Gilligan and Sam Clark, is a Series A–stage frontier-tech company operating in Housing & Construction. The company has raised $15M to date. The relevant peer set is sparse, comprising two private comparables (Inversion Space and Cobod) with no public housing-tech peers offering direct valuation anchors.

Valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. Using total capital raised ($15M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series A–to–next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.0x yields an implied post-money valuation of $30M. This method assumes Material Evolution will achieve standard progression milestones before Series B fundraising.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M (low) to $34M (high), with a median point estimate of $30M. Key uncertainties include the thinness of comparable data—only two private peers and zero public housing-construction peers limits confidence in relative-value cross-checks—and the assumption that standard step-up multiples apply to a frontier-tech subsector where capital efficiency and milestone achievement may diverge from median patterns. Further triangulation via revenue or EBITDA multiples would require operational metrics not provided here.
